artigo.texto: Residents of Jacumba Hot Springs gathered Monday night at the community center for their monthly Jacumba Community Sponsor Group meeting. But one agenda item dominated the discussion – preliminary plans for a data center north of Interstate 8. For years, back country residents in communities like Jacumba have fought large energy projects. Most recently, the Jacumba and Boulevard communities battled two solar and battery energy storage projects that the County Board of Supervisors ultimately approved. “At the end of the day, we’re going to represent ourselves at that table,” said Jeff Osborne, the community group’s current chair. “We’re going to ask for things. We’re gonna ask for representation. We hope to get some response on this specific topic of data centers from the supervisors soon so we can have some indication. Because this is kind of a whole new thing.” There are few things these days that have inflamed communities more than data centers. The massive buildings powering the AI boom can have huge impacts on local land use, water and power. “I’m pro business. I was a contractor for 30 years. But something like that out here in the mountains,” said Ray Tiffany, a longtime Jacumba resident. “It’s just not right.” Osborne first heard about the data center plans after members of the Boulevard Community Planning Group were tipped off by a local landowner. The Jacumba group confirmed the proposal through County records obtained under the California Public Records Act. The tentative plans come from the Spain-based renewable energy company, IGNIS. Tahir Fazal, an IGNIS representative, said in an interview with KPBS that the company is in the early phases of deciding whether to do the project. “We have not done an application, so this project right now is nothing more than a consultation to the county to assess what the permitting path will be, to assess whether there are any limitations that are in place for this project,” Fazal said. Fazal said if the company does decide to pursue the project, it will do community outreach. “We're gonna be transparent on this, as we progress, with the community,” Fazal said. “Right now, I cannot give you an accurate answer on when we will take action on the application. As I mentioned, we are evaluating the guidelines that we received.” The project would ultimately need approval from the San Diego County Board of Supervisors, a county spokesperson confirmed Tuesday.

artigo.texto: Stanton annexation request raises residents’ questions about possible data center STANTON, Tenn. (WBBJ) - Wednesday evening a Stanton municipal planning commission meeting took place at Stanton town hall. Members of the community filled town hall with the intention of getting a better understanding on the city’s plans and to express concerns about possible data centers moving into their region. Thomas Stringer, Stanton landowner said, “That’s really why we’re all here, you know, just so we can be in the know and nothing gets swept under the rug.” Stanton’s planning commission agenda listed a public hearing and consideration of an annexation request for land owned by the Juanita Buchanan and children’s trust. The agenda describes the request as approximately 164 acres. Residents say they want clear answers about what is being proposed such as the real reason the area needs to be re-zoned as industrial. They say they are worried about the developments the re-zoning would bring and how it would impact their town. “This is our home, this is where we live. The proposed land is right behind my property, you know, I could throw a rock and hit it. So, if it does come in it will disrupt everything that we have worked so hard for,” continued Stringer Town hall was so full of Haywood county residents that many were even standing outside to hear what leaders had to say in response to their concerns. A data center has not been confirmed as the proposed use for the land. There will be another meeting held next week for further discussion and a possible vote on whether or not to approve the proposed annexation of the land. Copyright 2026 WBBJ. All rights reserved.

artigo.texto: Indonesia requires support from developed countries and private partnerships to ensure climate financing is accessible. Benefits for local communities are a key priority. 11 Nov 2026 10:47 WIB · Lingkungan AFP ANTALYA, KOMPAS – The Indonesian government has reaffirmed its readiness to actively develop the carbon market as a strategic instrument to accelerate climate action and mobilize sustainable financing. This initiative has moved beyond mere ambition and has entered a phase of tangible implementation, with the preparation of regulations for carbon economic value and the offering of high-integrity carbon projects to global investors. President's Special Envoy for Climate and Energy Hashim Djojohadikusumo emphasized that Indonesia's natural wealth, encompassing forests, peatlands, mangroves, and oceans, is not merely a collection of resources but a national heritage and a significant contribution to the health of the planet. To maximize this potential, the government is enhancing carbon market governance through Presidential Regulation No. 110 of 2025 and developing a national carbon unit registry system (SRUK) to ensure transparency and investment certainty. "Indonesia views the carbon market as a strategic instrument to accelerate climate action, achieve our NDC targets, and mobilize sustainable financing," Hashim emphasized in a keynote speech during the discussion session titled "Unlocking Indonesia's Carbon Market Potential for Climate Action and Sustainable Finance" on Tuesday (10/11/2026) at the Indonesian pavilion at the 31st Conference of the Parties to the Climate Change Convention (COP31) in Antalya, Turkey. Hashim added that the development of a credible carbon market must deliver tangible environmental benefits and attract long-term investments, with a key requirement being the availability of a robust monitoring, reporting, and verification (MRV) system. In the maritime sector, Deputy Minister of Marine Affairs and Fisheries Irwan Meilano emphasized the urgency of incorporating the ocean into climate solutions, given the long-standing impacts felt by fishing communities and coastal ecosystems. The Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries is currently working on reforesting 600,000 hectares of mangroves and optimizing seagrass beds as part of its efforts to mitigate and adapt to climate change. "The challenge before us is no longer ambition; it's implementation," Irwan said at the same event. As a tactical step, Irwan stated that the Ministry of Marine Affairs and Fisheries will soon issue derivative regulations to implement the national carbon policy. The ministry is scheduled to launch a ministerial regulation on the economic value of carbon on November 18-19. Simultaneously, the government will also present three candidate blue carbon project sites to potential partners and investors. Furthermore, Hashim and Irwan agreed that the commercialization and preservation of carbon ecosystems must not overlook the welfare of surrounding communities. Hashim emphasized that conservation and natural restoration must create meaningful economic opportunities for local residents living alongside these ecosystems. In line with this, Irwan also emphasized the importance of support from developed countries and private partnerships to ensure climate funding is easily accessible. "We need straightforward access to funding, support for mobilizing private investment, and partnerships that transform good projects into viable investment models, while ensuring that the benefits reach local communities," he stated. During a press conference on Tuesday, COP31 Negotiation Presidency Chris Bowen set an ambitious target to increase global electrification levels to 35 percent by 2035. This initiative is seen as an essential requirement and the only way to prevent global temperatures from rising more than 1.5 degrees Celsius amid the threats of a global polycrisis. "We are meeting in a time of polycrisis, when the world is under immense pressure. Unlike previous COPs, we are now confronted with the rise of artificial intelligence and the pressures it places on energy networks. At the same time, the climate crisis has not disappeared; in fact, it is worsening," Bowen stated. Coinciding with Energy and Transport Day at COP31, Bowen emphasized the importance of accelerating electrification as a key solution to various crises. Currently, the global electrification rate stands at just 23 percent, a slow increase from 17 percent in 2005 and 19 percent in 2015. For years, the global electrification rate has increased by an average of only 0.3 percent per year. To achieve a leap target of 35 percent within less than a decade, the COP31 presidency is urging participating countries to sign an electrification pledge and engage in consultations to ensure this target is included in the conference's final decision. We want people to leave here saying, ‘Yes, things changed at COP31.’ Murat Kurum, COP31 President COP31 President Murat Kurum emphasized during the same press conference that electrification is a central theme of COP31. The presidency is advocating for the expanded use of clean energy-based electricity in the transportation, building, and industrial sectors to reduce dependence on the vulnerability of supply and prices of imported fossil fuels. The crisis in the global energy market has served as a harsh lesson for many countries. According to Kurum, from March to August 2026, fuel-importing nations will face an additional cost surge of approximately $330 billion due to price volatility. With the increasing affordability of electrical technology, electrification is seen as a golden opportunity to enhance energy security while also reducing emissions. artigo.texto: Wichita-area data center rules remain under review after a committee takes no action WICHITA, Kan. (KWCH) — A committee considering proposed data center regulations for Wichita and Sedgwick County took no action Thursday, postponing the matter until its next meeting in December. The Advance Plans Committee discussed a proposal that includes multiple annual air quality reports, plans to minimize noise, and water and energy usage plans. Dozens of people spoke during the meeting, and some said the proposed regulations did not go far enough. Adam May, who lives in Garden Plain, called for zoning boundaries to protect farmland from large data centers. “Growth is good but preservation is vital,” May said. “I think our zoning codes for hyperscale data centers must have clear boundaries that prevent them from swallowing up multi-generational farmland that defines the rural character of Sedgwick County.” Andale resident Holly Martin called for a 10-megawatt limit, saying the county should not become an “open season zone” for data center development. Sedgwick County currently has an interim moratorium on data center applications through December 24, 2026, while county planners work to establish the permanent zoning and land-use regulations. Durante a atividade, os estudantes foram recebidos por Raylan Matias, técnico em Telecomunicações, que apresentou o funcionamento da estrutura e compartilhou informações sobre os sistemas de redes de computadores e o grande volume de dados que circula diariamente por essas redes. A visita foi marcada por muito aprendizado, troca de conhecimentos e curiosidade. Os alunos tiveram a oportunidade de esclarecer dúvidas, conhecer de perto uma fibra óptica e compreender melhor a infraestrutura tecnológica que possibilita a transmissão de informações e a conexão entre diferentes sistemas. A experiência proporcionou uma aproximação entre os conteúdos estudados em sala de aula e a realidade do mercado de trabalho, especialmente na área de Redes de Computadores, componente curricular ministrado pelo professor Ailvan Silva. Mais do que conhecer equipamentos e estruturas, os estudantes puderam ampliar seus conhecimentos e perceber, na prática, a importância das redes de computadores para o funcionamento da sociedade conectada. (Viviane Fialho/Ascom IFPA Conceição)

artigo.texto: Ethiopia Backs Global Carbon Market Push as Forest Credit Deals Remain Unsigned #EBR_News Nov 12, 2026 Ethiopia, which will host COP32 in 2027, has joined China and Türkiye in launching a global initiative to strengthen cooperation on carbon crediting markets, even as its own efforts to turn forest carbon into revenue are still waiting to reach the deal-making stage. The initiative was unveiled on Wednesday at the 31st United Nations Climate Change Conference (COP31) in the Turkish coastal city of Antalya, Xinhua reported. According to Xinhua, the launch took place at the COP31 China Pavilion and was attended by government officials and representatives of international organisations, including the United Nations and the World Bank. COP31 opened on Monday and runs until Nov. 20, with representatives from nearly 200 countries and regions taking part, the news agency said. The initiative’s document calls on governments and intergovernmental bodies to improve governance systems for high-integrity carbon credits, Xinhua reported. It encourages cooperation among carbon crediting mechanisms and market participants to promote a high-integrity supply of credits, and calls for the responsible use of those credits to generate effective market demand. It also urges parties to enhance information sharing and the interconnectivity of market infrastructure. The three countries noted that carbon crediting mechanisms help optimise the allocation of mitigation resources, channel climate finance and unlock new drivers of green development. Li Gao, China’s vice minister of ecology and environment, said the initiative is guided by fairness, inclusiveness and voluntary participation, and is open to all. “We welcome governments, international organisations and relevant institutions to join us in delivering a new global public good for climate action,” Li said, according to Xinhua. Fatma Varank, Turkish deputy minister of environment, urbanisation and climate change, told Xinhua the initiative would give emerging economies a platform for South-South collaboration. She noted that developing countries often face financial and technical constraints in establishing and operating carbon markets, and said partnerships formed directly among such countries are especially valuable. Selam Kidane (PhD), chief strategist for Ethiopia’s COP32 Presidency, thanked the Chinese government for proposing the initiative and described it as an important platform for international cooperation on climate solutions. She said Ethiopia was pleased to join China and other partners in co-sponsoring and launching the initiative, describing it as an important platform for strengthening international cooperation on climate solutions. Cristina Reis, extraordinary secretary of carbon markets at Brazil’s Ministry of Finance, also welcomed the move, telling Xinhua that bridging voluntary and compliance carbon markets is essential to driving corporate emissions reductions. Ethiopia has also been laying the groundwork for forest carbon trading. As EBR reported reported in June, the country has put a legal framework for forest carbon trading in place through Forest Carbon Trading Directive No. 1122/2025, which allows forest owners and project developers to register carbon credit projects and jurisdictional programmes. Under the directive, communities engaged in state forest co-management are entitled to 80 per cent of revenue proceeds. The House of Peoples’ Representatives approved the directive on 30 June, the same day it was discussed at the Second Agriculture Science Seminar Series. In May, the Council of Ministers also approved a draft Carbon Market Proclamation aimed at operationalising carbon trading, revenue sharing and international transactions. Yet turning that readiness into revenue has proved slower. Speaking at the seminar, Motuma Tolera (PhD), Head of the Forest Sector Transformation Unit at the Ethiopian Forestry Development, said the Oromia Forested Landscape Program (OFLP) was still in “advanced negotiations” after more than a year of market outreach. According to Motuma, potential revenue could reach $200 million if CORSIA-eligible certification is achieved, but the figure remains provisional and depends on securing international buyers and meeting stringent standards. CORSIA is the International Civil Aviation Organization’s offsetting scheme, where credits have traded at a premium of $10 to $20 per tonne over the past year, he said. Motuma added that the programme engaged more than 25 prospective buyers across three continents before narrowing talks to a shortlist of traders and intermediaries. He also said the ISFL standard was approved for CORSIA use only in April, and that the National Jurisdictional Forest Carbon Program, being registered under the ART-TREES methodology, is still in validation. Ethiopia holds 26.75 million hectares of forest, equal to 23.6 per cent of its land cover, according to Motuma, which points to substantial carbon stock potential. The experience of the Humbo and Sodo reforestation projects, started in 2006, shows how long the road can be: they have sequestered 462,606 tonnes of carbon dioxide equivalent and channelled $1.63 million to community cooperatives over two decades. Its emphasis on high-integrity supply, responsible demand and connected market infrastructure mirrors buyers’ growing insistence on rigorously verified credits, which the directive itself reflects by requiring independent, internationally accredited verification and ten-year record keeping. Those requirements raise costs, particularly for smaller projects, so a South-South platform that shares information and pools technical experience could help. With COP32 due to be hosted in Ethiopia in 2027, the country has a visible stake in how such markets are shaped, and also a reputational incentive to show that its carbon framework can deliver real transactions by then.

artigo.texto: Event The EBRD at COP31 COP31 will take place between 9 November and 20 November 2025 in Antalya, Turkiye 20 Nov 2026 Who we are Overview: about the EBRD Explore the EBRD’s journey over the decades, investing in businesses, supporting economies and driving lasting change across its regions. What we do Overview: how the EBRD operates Across three continents, the EBRD supports the transition to successful market economies. Work with us Overview: how you can work with the EBRD We draw on three decades of regional knowledge and financial expertise to tailor our products and approaches to each client's needs. Author: Nibal Zgheib The European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) has signed a €50 million financing package with Société Tunisienne de l'Electricité et du Gaz (STEG) to finance a new solar power plant integrated with Tunisia’s first utility-scale battery energy storage system. The package consists of a €30 million EBRD sovereign-guaranteed loan to STEG, complemented by a €20 million concessional loan from the Climate Investment Funds’ (CIF) Clean Technology Fund (CTF). Under the Global Energy Storage Program, the CTF’s concessional financing makes the investment more affordable, and supports the deployment of battery storage technology in Tunisia. Located in Beni Mhira in the southern governorate of Tataouine, the project will comprise a 50 MWac solar photovoltaic plant integrated with a 10 MW/20 MWh battery energy storage system. It will also include a 1.2 km high-voltage transmission line connecting the facility to the national grid. Integrating solar generation with battery storage will increase the flexibility of Tunisia’s power system as more renewable capacity comes online. As the country’s first utility-scale battery storage project, the investment, supported by EBRD technical cooperation, will also help STEG to develop the technical and operational capabilities needed to integrate storage into the national grid. Aida Sitdikova, Director of Sustainable Infrastructure, Middle East and Africa, said: “Tunisia has outstanding solar potential, and storage will help the country to make greater use of it. This first utility-scale battery is an important milestone for Tunisia's energy security and its energy transition. Beyond the asset itself, it will help build the experience and frameworks needed for further storage projects, including private-sector investments.” Faycel Tarifa, Chief Executive Officer of STEG said: “This project marks a new chapter for STEG and for Tunisia’s power system. As our grid takes on more renewable energy, the ability to store and dispatch it becomes essential to keep supply secure and reliable. With Tunisia’s first utility-scale battery, STEG will build the know-how to operate storage at scale and integrate it into the national grid. We thank the EBRD and the Clean Technology Fund for their continued trust and support in this important step.” The project is part of STEG’s wider programme to develop 380 MWac of solar generation capacity and 100 MWh of battery storage, and is aligned with Tunisia’s efforts to diversify its energy mix and reduce its dependence on imported fossil fuels. It builds on the EBRD’s longstanding support for Tunisia’s power sector, including grid reinforcement, the first large-scale private renewable energy projects and the ELMED electricity interconnector between Tunisia and Italy. The EBRD is one of Tunisia’s leading institutional investors. Since the start of its operations in the country in 2012, the Bank has invested more than €3.3 billion in over 100 projects there. artigo.texto: Westlake approves agreement, clearing way for controversial North Texas data center A controversial data center project in Westlake will move forward after the Town Council approved a development agreement Thursday, following a recent settlement reached by the developer, the city of Keller and nearby homeowners. The approval clears the way for construction to begin near U.S. Highway 377 and Westport Parkway, following months of delays, legal challenges, and opposition from some residents. According to Westlake officials, the data center will cover nearly 88 acres and is expected to generate about $5 million annually for the town during its first 10 years. Thursday's presentation on the data center is available here. Keller homeowners' concerns lead to additional protections Earlier this month, Keller city leaders approved a settlement with Westlake and developer Circle T Owner LP. The agreement includes noise restrictions, environmental safeguards, and other protections for nearby residents. The nearly $2 million settlement provides $1.5 million for noise monitoring and other programs, $300,000 for Keller Fire Rescue, and additional money to cover legal and consulting expenses. Homeowners in Keller's Marshall Ridge neighborhood had opposed the project, saying they were blindsided by plans to build the massive data center just a few hundred feet from their properties. Concerns about noise, environmental impacts, and the approval process led to lawsuits and a temporary court order blocking Westlake from advancing the project's development agreement. The order was later dissolved. The homeowners also agreed to settle their lawsuit. The dispute strained relations between Keller and Westlake. Westlake voted against renewing its police services contract with Keller. The existing contract runs through October 2028. Under the settlement, Keller gains contractual rights to enforce certain noise, screening, and operational requirements at the site, even though the property is outside Keller city limits. According to the City of Keller, the settlement includes: - Noise restrictions: Daytime and nighttime noise limits at residential property lines, an independent baseline noise study, and quarterly monitoring for three years after operations begin. - Landscaping: A 10-foot landscaping berm to help screen the facility from nearby neighborhoods. Trees that die or sustain significant damage affecting their screening function must be replaced. - Community funding: A $1.5 million contribution for noise monitoring, environmental mitigation, and other municipal programs and services benefiting Keller residents. - Fire protection: A $300,000 contribution toward Keller Fire Rescue training, equipment, decontamination, and other emergency response costs associated with the project. - Generator restrictions: Diesel-powered backup generators must have EPA Tier 4 emissions controls, with generator testing limited to daytime hours. - Grading and drainage: Circle T must provide the project's grading plan, including the proposed berm and related drainage improvements. - Legal expenses: A $76,000 payment toward Keller's attorney fees and expert consultant costs. Data centers become a political issue in Texas The Westlake dispute comes amid growing opposition to artificial intelligence data centers across Texas and other states, with concerns about electricity costs, water consumption and the effects on surrounding communities becoming issues in the Nov. 3 midterm elections. According to Cleanview Research, 75% of data centers under construction in the United States and 80% of planned projects are in predominantly Republican states. Texas leads the nation in data centers under construction. In September, Gov. Greg Abbott directed state regulators to halt environmental permits and other regulatory approvals for data center projects pending an audit of their potential impact on the state's electric grid. The issue also became part of the Texas governor's race. Democrat Gina Hinojosa, who campaigned against the rapid expansion of data centers, defeated Abbott in the Nov. 3 election. President Donald Trump has supported data center development, citing its importance to economic growth and national security. But public opposition has grown, with some Republican leaders, including Abbott, taking steps to restrict new projects. CBS News Texas will provide updates as more information becomes available.

artigo.texto: Bidirectional charging: Audi A2 e-tron as a mobile energy storage system The high-voltage battery of an electric car can not only provide the energy for driving, but can also be used specifically as a power source beyond the road. With bidirectional charging functions, the Audi A2 e-tron enables external devices to be supplied via Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) and the use of stored energy in the household via Vehicle-to-Home (V2H). In the future, Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) will be added for feeding energy back into the public power grid. Key facts at a glance - New Audi A2 e-tron available to order in three battery variants (52, 61 and 84 kWh) - DC charging power from 100 to 183 kWh - DC charging from 10 to 80 percent in 24 to 29 minutes - Vehicle-to-Load (V2L) and Vehicle-to-Home (V2H) expand the use of the high-voltage battery - Vehicle-to-grid (V2G) will enable energy to be fed into the public power grid in the future Battery system with coordinated thermal management and charging electronics Focus on thermal management and charging efficiency DC charging and integrated charging electronics The following table provides an overview of the charging time for DC charging from 10 to 80 percent filling status of the battery, depending on the respective model variant and battery capacity. The specified charging times apply under defined test conditions. The actual charging time may depend on battery temperature, state of charge and available charging power, among other things. The battery in the A2 e-tron is not only designed for a short-term power peak. The focus for everyday use is on a plannable, controlled and usable charging process. For this purpose, an advanced component is used that combines on-board chargers and DC/DC converters, the so-called OCDC 2.0. It includes a higher number of metal-oxide-semiconductor field-effect transistors (MOSFETs), adapted AC output management and corresponding software adjustments. Battery management A battery management controller takes over the monitoring and regulation of the battery. In LFP batteries in particular, a flatter Open Circuit Voltage (OCV) characteristic curve of the cells makes it more difficult to precisely determine the state of charge and aging. For this reason, Audi uses an adapted algorithm. The information obtained is incorporated into the calculation of range, charging behavior and operating strategy. Extended energy use The battery in the A2 e-tron is not only used as an energy storage system for driving, but can also generate additional benefits outside the vehicle, depending on the application. Vehicle-to-Load(V2L) makes it possible to supply suitable external consumers with electrical energy via the vehicle. This makes the A2 e-tron a mobile and flexible energy source. The Vehicle-to-Home (V2H) function uses the A2 e-tron as a large battery storage system and, in conjunction with a compatible, bidirectional DC wallbox, makes it possible to use the stored electricity for the household. Depending on the market, vehicle equipment, compatible charging infrastructure, home installation, regulatory requirements and, if necessary, a suitable electricity tariff, the compact Audi will enable Vehicle-to-Grid (V2G) in the future. Energy from the vehicle battery is provided for the public power grid. This makes the battery part of a larger energy system. Conclusion With the A2 e-tron, Audi is pursuing the goal of making electric mobility in the compact segment suitable for everyday use, efficient and flexible. The interplay of coordinated thermal management, intelligent charging electronics and advanced battery management ensures stable and reproducible charging behavior. At the same time, bidirectional charging functions extend the battery's range of application beyond driving and thus make the vehicle an active part of the energy system. In this way, the A2 e-tron combines efficient charging, intelligent energy use and a high level of everyday usability in a future-oriented overall concept. Animation: Audi A2 e-tron - Battery technology and bidirectional charging Frequently Asked Questions What does bidirectional charging mean? Bidirectional charging means that an electric car can not only absorb electricity from the grid, but also return it. This turns the vehicle into a flexible energy source. What can be charged? With bidirectional charging, it does not matter whether an external device is charged (Vehicle-to-Load; V2L), a house is supplied with electricity (Vehicle-to-Home; V2H) or energy is fed into the public power grid in the future (Vehicle-to-Grid; V2G).

artigo.texto: BYD Is Combining Solar Energy Storage, Five-Minute Flash Charging, And Robotic Arms For Its New Charging Stations Despite not selling any cars in the U.S., China's BYD is quietly taking over the EV world. It has surpassed Tesla as the world's largest electric carmaker by global sales, and it's also been hard at work trying to dethrone Tesla as the provider of the world's most advanced EV charging network. Now it's announced the latest big step toward that goal. On Tuesday, BYD announced that it will combine clean solar power, its proprietary Flash Charging tech that uses local energy storage, and robotic arms into one EV charging system. The core of this system is BYD's Flash Charging, which draws power from the grid like any other EV charging station. Unlike others, though, it stores the electricity in two on-site 185-kilowatt batteries. That stored energy can then be pumped into your EV way quicker than it would be if it were drawing from the grid directly, BYD says. Each Flash Charger has two connectors, capable of up to 1,500 kW charging if only one is in use, or 1,000 kW if two cars are sharing. For context, Tesla's new V4 Superchargers top out at 500 kW, regular superchargers hit 250 kW, and the fastest DC chargers from Electrify America can do 350 kW. BYD's quoted charge times are 10% to 70% in five minutes, 10% to 97% in nine minutes, and in cold weather, 20% to 97% in 12 minutes given an ambient temperature of minus 30 degrees Fahrenheit. Solar-powered arms race BYD is now incorporating solar generation into the equation, drawing power from the sun to those same local 185-kW batteries, presumably via solar panels placed on top of the charging station's canopy. This means the system is less reliant on the grid, which is huge in remote, sun-soaked regions like, say, the desert in the United Arab Emirates where BYD launched all this. Then there are the robotic arms. The idea is far from new or original — Tesla promised them a decade ago, and EV makers like Volkswagen, Hyundai, and China's Xiaomi have since built their own renditions. It's a simple premise: A robotic arm locates your car's charging port, opens the cover, and inserts the connector automatically. BYD plans to install 6,000 Flash Charging stations worldwide by the end of next year. Don't expect all or even most of them to get solar power or the robot arms initially, but if BYD can actually normalize five-minute charging with solar and robot arms sometime in the next couple of years, we might be looking at the new charging network king.

artigo.texto: Frontier Institute announces lawsuit against Missoula’s data center zoning ordinance MISSOULA, Mont. — On Nov. 9, Frontier Institute announced attorneys from Arizona’s Goldwater Institute will represent CubCloud AI in a lawsuit regarding Missoula’s zoning regulations after the city passed an ordinance in October that would change the way it zones for data centers. “There’s a lot of things we should be requiring of data centers, I just don’t believe that what we’re doing should be in the same category of a multibillion-dollar facility,” Joshua Rhines, founder and CEO of CubCloud AI, said. The ordinance adopted by Missoula simply changed what is defined by a data center in regard to zoning. “It currently reads as a facility or portion of a facility housing network computer systems, servers and appliances and telecommunications equipment. It goes on. I simply would like to or propose that it read and slash or telecommunications,” Justin Ponton, the ward 2 city council member, said when he proposed the amendment back in October. The ordinance passed unanimously, and the addition of that one word may place protections on high-scale data centers. But, according to the lawsuit, it violates Montana’s Right to Compute Act and jeopardizes small tech businesses and their ability to grow in Montana. “Lawmakers go about regulating for data centers they need to make sure that they’re being thoughtful in the way they go about it. They can’t just enact sweeping bans on an entire category of technology without potentially sweeping in the little guys and these local small businesses like CubCloud who are real assets to our community,” Kendall Cotton, CEO and president of Frontier Institute, said. CubCloud AI is a local Missoula tech company founded on the belief that Montana had a need for local AI infrastructure and provides local organizations looking to implement AI an alternative to large-scale data centers like Microsoft or Meta. “You know it was never going to be like a hyperscale data center that would be 20 megawatts like Bonner or 100 megawatts or any of that it always planned to be like 2 or 3, you know obviously those plans are off the table right now you until we figure out what’s going on with ordinance here,” Rhines said. The city is aware of the lawsuit and issued this statement to NBC Montana regarding its current stance. It reads: “The city is aware of the lawsuit filed by CubCloud, however it has not been served the lawsuit as of the present moment. The city is aware of the Right to Compute Act. It is the city’s position that the Right to Compute Act does not give data center companies the right to locate wherever they please. The city plans to vigorously defend the City Council decision in this case. However, the city will not comment on the specifics of this case pending litigation.” CubCloud AI is not seeking a monetary settlement and simply is looking to work with the city to revise the current ordinance. “Our hope is we can have a productive dialogue and hopefully come out with an ordinance that addresses small business interest and saves the city from getting a Trojan horse situation which I think is probably why they passed the ordinance and their main fear,” Rhines said.

artigo.texto: A Eletronet, uma empresa Axia Energia, referência em telecomunicações e TI, anuncia o ELET1, seu novo Data Center em São Paulo, que ampliará a oferta de serviços de colocation, Conectividade e interconexão da companhia e fornecerá mais escala ao atendimento de provedores de nuvem, operadoras de telecomunicações e Provedores de Internet (ISPs), e hyperscalers. Com investimento de R$ 25 milhões, o centro terá aproximadamente 350 m², capacidade para cerca de 90 racks e potência inicial de 0,5 MW, podendo chegar a 1 MW na segunda fase de expansão. Com as obras já iniciadas, a previsão de lançamento é para o primeiro trimestre de 2027. O projeto acompanha o aumento da procura de empresas dos segmentos de Cloud, streaming e telecomunicações por infraestrutura de Data Center em regiões estratégicas de São Paulo, com alta disponibilidade e acesso a um amplo ecossistema de conteúdo. O ELET1 estará em uma localização com elevada concentração de redes de telecomunicações e provedores de conteúdo. O Data Center também abrigará o PIX (Ponto de Interconexão) da Eletronet no IX.br São Paulo, ponto de troca de tráfego de Internet do mundo, tanto em volume quanto em número de participantes. O PIX da companhia se destaca por liderar o volume de tráfego de download entre as operadoras participantes do IX.br São Paulo. Para os clientes, estar nesse ambiente aumenta as possibilidades de conexão com diferentes redes e provedores de serviços digitais. “O ELET1 representa um passo estratégico para fortalecer nossa atuação no segmento de Data Centers. Estamos ampliando nossa estrutura para atender às necessidades dos clientes que já utilizam nossos serviços e abrir novas oportunidades de negócios, em um contexto no qual a hiperconectividade e a disponibilidade se tornam cada vez mais essenciais”, afirma Rogerio Garchet, CEO da Eletronet. Segundo ele, o projeto acompanha o avanço de aplicações em Nuvem, Inteligência Artificial, streaming e serviços digitais, que exigem suporte para volumes cada vez maiores de Dados. “Queremos ir além das necessidades atuais e antecipar os próximos ciclos do mercado, fortalecendo nossa capacidade de conectar clientes, redes e ecossistemas digitais”, diz. Com Segurança, tecnologia de última geração e resiliência operacional entre os pilares da iniciativa, o ELET1 seguirá as melhores práticas globais de infraestrutura, com soluções voltadas à proteção física e lógica, alinhadas às diretrizes da norma ISO 27001. O Data Center também contará com aplicações modernas e práticas de gestão ambiental e energética, tendo como referência os padrões ISO 14001, ISO 50001 e LEED, apoiando no melhor desempenho energético e na redução do PUE (Power Usage Effectiveness). Entre os recursos previstos estão dois geradores redundantes de 500 kVA, dupla entrada de rede, backbone DWDM protegido, sistema de gerenciamento predial (BMS) atualizado, monitoramento contínuo e um Centro de Operações de Rede (NOC) de contingência. “Mais capacidade precisa vir acompanhada de eficiência, resiliência e previsibilidade operacional. Por isso, o ELET1 foi concebido com uma arquitetura que otimiza o uso dos recursos e oferece mais flexibilidade à operação. A modernização dos sistemas críticos também nos permitirá atender a diferentes perfis de uso e níveis de demanda, mantendo o ambiente preparado para operações críticas”, afirma Emerson Hioki, diretor de Tecnologia(CTO) da Eletronet. O ELET1 integra a estratégia da Eletronet de fortalecer sua atuação em Data Centers e complementa a expansão de sua rede nacional de fibra óptica. A nova unidade também contempla a migração da infraestrutura atualmente instalada no Data Center da companhia em São Paulo para o novo ambiente, em um processo planejado para preservar a continuidade dos serviços. Serviço www.eletronet.com

artigo.texto: The Boulder County Board of Commissioners voted unanimously Tuesday to prohibit data centers using more than 50 kilowatts of power, banning all but the smallest facilities in unincorporated Boulder County. The new rule is among the most restrictive data center regulations in Colorado. This summer, Longmont banned only hyperscale data centers, which use far more power. Several cities, including Denver, Brighton, Lafayette, Littleton and Fort Collins, have imposed temporary moratoriums while they study the issue. Boulder County’s new rule follows its own six-month moratorium. Colorado has no statewide regulations specifically governing data center development. Lawmakers rejected bills that would have offered incentives for data centers or imposed new regulations in May but are expected to revisit the issue in 2027. The county’s decision comes amid growing opposition to data center development nationwide. About half of U.S. states have restrictions or moratoriums. In this month’s elections, voters backed measures limiting data center development in 40 of 41 local ballot initiatives. “We saw on Election Day around the country a message from Americans that they’re concerned about the regulation of big tech and the implications that that has on people’s lives, livelihoods and ability to thrive,” County Commissioner Ashley Stolzmann said. “Those similar implications that we heard across the country, we’ve heard in our community also.” Commissioners voiced concerns about data centers’ electricity and water consumption, noise pollution and emissions. Xcel Energy anticipates that new data centers will account for 62% of its projected energy growth. A Lawrence Berkeley National Lab study estimates that data centers could account for 6% to 12% of U.S. electricity consumption by 2028. A mid-sized data center uses around 300,000 gallons of water a day, about as much as 1,000 households. The new restriction applies to unincorporated Boulder County, not the City of Boulder or other municipalities. Data centers using 50 kilowatts or less would be allowed only in industrial zones. That’s a relatively small amount of power for a data center, enough to operate a facility ranging from a refrigerator-sized unit to a small server room. In the City of Boulder, hyperscale data centers are not specifically defined in the land-use code. Proposals would need to be evaluated individually, according to city planning spokesperson Cate Stanek. Generally, land uses not listed in the code are prohibited. Stanek said adding data centers to the code would require further study and “may be considered in 2027.” Commissioners approved the restriction despite a unanimous recommendation from the county Planning Commission to delay the decision. The advisory body urged more research and a joint work session before proceeding. “It just seems we’re not ready,” Planning Commissioner Rachel Lee said. The path to 50 kilowatts County staff began exploring changes to the land-use code in June after commissioners asked for ways to prohibit data centers. Staff proposed a 75-kilowatt limit, based on a definition from Energy Star, a federal energy efficiency program. “Once a server room reaches 75 kilowatts, it starts to resemble something like a data center,” county senior planner Ethan Abner told commissioners at a Nov. 10 meeting. He said power consumption provides a useful proxy for potential land-use impacts. Commissioner Marta Loachamin proposed lowering the threshold even further, to 50 kilowatts. “Fifty was the number that was coming to my mind. I don’t have a calculation,” she said, explaining that she wanted to account for impacts the county might not have considered. The other commissioners agreed to the lower limit, though Commissioner Claire Levy acknowledged uncertainty. “I don’t know that any of us knows it’s the right number,” she said of the 75-kilowatt limit. Stolzmann said the lower limit would provide a greater buffer against potential impacts. Not in our backyard? Before the vote, the county shared its proposal with local governments, boards and Xcel Energy. Only the City of Boulder shared feedback. Boulder Senior City Planner Chris Ranglos shared the county’s concerns about the environmental impacts, but also encouraged commissioners to consider the needs of Boulder’s growing quantum computing industry, which could benefit from local data centers. Boulder is home to more than 30 quantum companies and JILA, a leading quantum research institute operated jointly by CU Boulder and the National Institute of Standards and Technology. Some planning commissioners worried the restrictions could hurt local businesses while shifting the environmental impacts to neighboring communities. “We want to consume these things, but we want other communities and other places to be able to house and produce these things,” Planning Commissioner Bryan Kominek, executive director of a solar agricultural learning center, said. “It’s our community saying: ‘Not in our backyard, but it’s okay in other people’s backyards.’” Several planning commissioners argued that Boulder County would be better equipped to regulate data centers responsibly than neighboring jurisdictions. “Data centers are likely coming, whether we like it or not,” said Planning Commissioner Gavin McMillan, a planning and development consultant. “The way that this code is written, it basically bans them in Boulder County. “If we make it impossible to build them here, they are going to get built somewhere, and it’s probably going to be in a neighboring community.” Instead, he said, “we need to think about how we can be the model of how this happens here.” Stolzmann rejected the “not in my backyard” criticism, saying other municipalities “could and should” adopt similar regulations. “I think what we came up with is threading the needle, allowing for computing and technology but not rushing too quickly into unfettered access to data centers and huge facilities that can impact people

artigo.texto: JBNews Por José Teixeira O governador de Mato Grosso, Otaviano Pivetta, ampliou nesta quarta-feira (11) as articulações internacionais para atrair investimentos destinados à conservação ambiental no Estado. Durante a COP31, realizada na Turquia, ele se reuniu com representantes da Coalizão LEAF e da Emergent, duas importantes iniciativas de financiamento climático, para apresentar os avanços das políticas de controle do desmatamento e discutir as condições necessárias para que Mato Grosso ingresse no mercado internacional de créditos de carbono. A aproximação com os investidores ocorre em uma etapa estratégica para o governo estadual, que pretende conquistar a certificação internacional das reduções de emissões de gases de efeito estufa obtidas por meio da preservação florestal. A expectativa é concluir os procedimentos necessários em 2027 e, a partir disso, estabelecer contratos comerciais com compradores interessados em financiar resultados ambientais comprovados. A Coalizão LEAF, iniciativa de financiamento voltada à proteção de florestas tropicais, reúne governos e empresas interessados na aquisição de reduções verificadas de emissões. Entre os países participantes estão o Reino Unido e a Noruega. Já a Emergent atua na intermediação e mobilização de recursos para transações de créditos florestais de alta integridade ambiental. O encontro coloca Mato Grosso em contato com organizações que possuem capacidade de mobilizar volumes expressivos de capital internacional. Para o governo, essa interlocução é importante porque permite apresentar diretamente aos potenciais compradores os resultados das políticas ambientais desenvolvidas no território estadual, além de esclarecer os requisitos técnicos e institucionais para futuras operações comerciais. Durante a reunião, Pivetta detalhou a trajetória de construção do programa de Redução de Emissões por Desmatamento e Degradação Florestal em escala jurisdicional, conhecido como REDD+ Jurisdicional. O mecanismo permite que governos estaduais comprovem a diminuição das emissões decorrentes da perda de vegetação nativa e, mediante certificação, negociem esses resultados com financiadores internacionais. O governador também apresentou a evolução do modelo produtivo mato-grossense e das medidas de acompanhamento do uso da terra, defendendo a continuidade das políticas públicas que buscam conciliar a expansão econômica com a proteção dos recursos naturais. A posição apresentada aos investidores é de que o Estado pretende manter a competitividade de sua produção agropecuária sem abandonar os compromissos ambientais. A estratégia ganha relevância porque Mato Grosso abriga áreas da Amazônia, do Cerrado e do Pantanal, três biomas que concentram importantes desafios de conservação, fiscalização e prevenção de danos ambientais. A secretária estadual de Meio Ambiente, Mauren Lazzaretti, que acompanha as negociações, apresentou o cronograma necessário para que os compromissos discutidos na conferência possam avançar para a etapa comercial. Segundo ela, três providências devem ser concluídas em 2027: a estruturação da Companhia Mato-grossense de Ativos Ambientais S.A. (CMAA), a realização das consultas relacionadas às salvaguardas socioambientais e a certificação internacional dos créditos de carbono pelo padrão ART-TREES. A futura companhia estadual terá papel relevante na organização e na negociação dos ativos ambientais. A proposta é criar uma estrutura específica para administrar os instrumentos econômicos ligados à conservação, facilitando o relacionamento com compradores e investidores. As consultas de salvaguardas, por sua vez, são necessárias para assegurar que o programa respeite critérios sociais e ambientais, inclusive os direitos e a participação das comunidades envolvidas nas políticas de conservação. Essa etapa integra as exigências internacionais para conferir legitimidade às reduções de emissões que poderão ser comercializadas. Outro requisito é a certificação ART-TREES, padrão internacional utilizado para avaliar e reconhecer reduções de emissões provenientes do desmatamento e da degradação florestal em escala estadual ou nacional. O procedimento exige mecanismos de monitoramento, contabilização e verificação dos resultados apresentados pelos governos. Sem essas etapas, Mato Grosso ainda não poderá transformar o interesse demonstrado pelos investidores em contratos de compra e venda de carbono certificados pelo programa. A previsão apresentada pela Secretaria de Meio Ambiente é que o Estado chegue à próxima conferência internacional do clima com as condições jurídicas, institucionais e técnicas necessárias para formalizar as primeiras operações. Embora o encontro tenha aproximado o governo de potenciais compradores, ainda não foram anunciados valores, quantidades de créditos ou contratos resultantes da reunião de quarta-feira. O avanço efetivo das negociações dependerá da certificação das reduções de emissões e das condições comerciais estabelecidas com os investidores. A movimentação diplomática de Pivetta durante a COP31 demonstra que o governo estadual está direcionando parte de sua agenda ambiental para a atração de capital estrangeiro. A estratégia pretende fazer da conservação florestal uma atividade capaz de gerar receitas para financiar novas políticas públicas, ao mesmo tempo em que fortalece a posição de Mato Grosso nas negociações internacionais sobre mudanças climáticas. O resultado concreto dessa articulação deverá ser conhecido em 2027, prazo estabelecido pela própria administração estadual para concluir as etapas que permitirão transformar as reduções certificadas de emissões em negócios no mercado internacional de carbono.

artigo.texto: A computational and experimental investigation of calcium-iron-manganese oxide perovskites has revealed that tailoring iron concentrations to lean levels yields a notable surge in chemical energy storage capacity, surpassing standard benchmark materials under identical operating conditions. In research detailing the redox behavior of CaFexMn1-xO3-δ across its full compositional range, an iron-lean formulation containing approximately six and a quarter percent iron achieved an energetic thermochemical storage density of fifty-three kilojoules per mole of oxygen when reduced at twelve hundred and fifty degrees Celsius and re-oxidized at seven hundred and sixty degrees Celsius. This chemical capacity exceeds that of the established state-of-the-art comparator material, calcium aluminum manganese oxide, by approximately twenty percent under identical thermal and atmospheric boundaries. The storage potential peaked at sixty kilojoules per mole across an expanded temperature divergence of eight hundred and fifty degrees Celsius, establishing iron-lean compositions as exceptionally effective media for capturing and releasing high-grade thermal energy through cyclical chemical transformations. The search for resilient energy storage technologies stems directly from the expanding diversification of renewable generation and the fundamental intermittency challenges that afflict clean power infrastructure. Renewable sources including solar photovoltaic panels, wind turbine arrays, and concentrated solar thermal plants experience environmental fluctuations that disrupt steady electricity delivery, impair load-following capabilities, and create severe supply-demand mismatches across distribution networks. Thermal energy storage systems serve as critical operational buffers by holding surplus generation as thermal energy for dispatch into downstream industrial processes or thermal power generation cycles. While traditional sensible heat storage materials absorb energy via plain temperature elevations without changing phase and reach volumetric storage densities of around two hundred megajoules per cubic meter, latent storage media exploit phase changes to achieve three hundred to five hundred megajoules per cubic meter. In contrast, thermochemical energy storage operates through reversible chemical reactions without undergoing destructive structural melting, offering superior reported theoretical and experimental energy densities spanning 0.5 to 3 gigajoules per cubic meter. Thermochemical energy storage in redox-active metal oxides operates via a closed two-step thermochemical cycle that stores thermal input directly within reversible chemical bonds. During the charging stage, high-temperature heat drives the endothermic reduction of the metal oxide lattice, freeing oxygen gas from the crystalline framework and generating vacancies across the anionic sublattice. During the subsequent discharge cycle, ambient or compressed air streams flow across the reduced material, initiating an exothermic re-oxidation that takes up oxygen into the vacant sites and releases the stored chemical enthalpy as high-temperature heat. Unlike systems that undergo crystallographic phase shifts across distinct solid phases, vacancy-driven perovskite frameworks maintain structural integrity through cyclical bond formation while offering high reaction enthalpies and exceptional physical durability. Iron substitution within calcium manganese oxide systems presents an attractive route to calibrate reaction thermodynamics, because replacing expensive cobalt modifiers with abundant iron significantly suppresses raw material expenses while tuning the operational enthalpy of reduction across demanding thermal envelopes. Despite the recognized theoretical advantages of the calcium-iron-manganese oxide family, substantial information gaps previously hindered the deployment and optimization of these perovskites in high-temperature storage systems. Prior thermodynamic evaluations were restricted to a single linearized van ‘t Hoff modeling investigation that surveyed only three isolated iron concentrations, leaving the vast majority of the compositional spectrum uncharacterized. Linearized van ‘t Hoff approximations introduce significant compounding errors, impose rigid assumptions regarding temperature-independent enthalpies and entropies, and cannot continuously predict the thermodynamic consequences of complex cation-cation interactions. Consequently, the temperature dependence of enthalpy, entropy, and non-stoichiometry remained unknown across broad operating regimes. To resolve this deficiency, researchers implemented the advanced CrossFit Compound Energy Formalism algorithm, a thermodynamic modeling architecture capable of integrating theoretical quantum simulations with empirical thermal measurements to yield continuous, temperature-dependent, and composition-dependent representations of metal oxide reduction and re-oxidation behavior without relying on simplifying linearity assumptions. The CrossFit Compound Energy Formalism constructs an analytical solution model for the system free energy by unifying the distinct thermodynamic contributions of endmember configurations, configurational entropy, and excess interaction expressions. In the formulation developed for the calcium-iron-manganese system, calcium cations exclusively occupy the A-sublattice, while the B-sublattice incorporates four distinct transition metal species representing trivalent and tetravalent manganese alongside trivalent and tetravalent iron. The associated oxygen sublattice accommodates divalent oxygen anions alongside neutral oxygen vacancies. Site-fraction equations were mathematically derived from iron concentrations and the degree of oxygen off-stoichiometry, reflecting an equal distribution of reduction charge across active transition metal sites. artigo.texto: Política de minerais críticos vai priorizar imãs, baterias e fertilizantes Secretário de Mineração sinaliza cadeias que serão classificadas como prioritárias para liberação de instrumentos fiscais e de financiamento O Cimce (Conselho Nacional para Industrialização de Minerais Críticos e Estratégicos) deve enquadrar como prioritárias para a nova Política Nacional de Minerais Críticos as cadeias de imãs, baterias e fertilizantes, sinalizou nesta 4ª feira (11.nov.2026) o secretário nacional de Geologia, Mineração e Transformação Mineral do MME (Ministério de Minas e Energia), Anderson Arruda. O governo deve definir na próxima reunião do conselho, no final de novembro, as cadeias de minerais que receberão prioridade na aplicação dos instrumentos de financiamento e benefícios fiscais criados pela nova política. “Se a gente for pegar os debates que têm sido feitos sobre os projetos estratégicos, são esses: ímãs, baterias e fertilizantes. Obviamente, o Ministério de Minas e Energia e o Mdic [Ministério do Desenvolvimento, Indústria, Comércio e Serviços], a gente está estudando, vendo quais são as outras cadeias que a gente pode atender também”, disse Arruda a jornalistas após participação no seminário “Fertilizantes: da dependência externa à resiliência do agro brasileiro”, organizado pelo Poder360, em Brasília. Segundo o secretário, a discussão sobre as cadeias levará em conta a demanda nacional pelos produtos que têm como matéria-prima os minerais classificados como prioritários na lista aprovada na 1ª reunião do Conselho. Questionado sobre eventual mudança na configuração da lista, Arruda disse não ver como “factível” que alterações sejam feitas agora. Como mostrou o Poder360, o Ibram (Instituto Brasileiro de Mineração) pediu uma revisão da relação para subir o potássio e o fosfato da classe 2 para a classe 1. Os minerais são matéria-prima para o setor de fertilizantes. “Não adianta a gente ter 27 minerais e não ter projeto. E agora, o governo vai se debruçar sobre essa carteira de projetos do Brasil. Quais são os projetos de maturidade, por exemplo, para ter um daqueles instrumentos [de financiamento e crédito fiscal]? Isso eu tenho falado para o setor de fertilizante. Houve uma seleção de classes, mas isso não quer dizer que o fertilizante não seja prioritário”, disse o secretário. URÂNIO FICA SEPARADO Arruda voltou a afirmar que o mineral será debatido separadamente das outras cadeias, por estar sob regime de monopólio da União e por demandar investimento público. Segundo o secretário, o Brasil tem alto potencial de desenvolver o setor em curto prazo, por ter reservas e tecnologia para transformar o mineral em combustível nuclear. “A gente já tem a cadeia adensada no Brasil e a gente já tem a demanda que é Angra 1 e 2 e possivelmente Angra 3. Então, a gente tem reserva, demanda e tecnologia. No curto prazo, a gente consegue inclusive atender esse interesse do presidente Lula, que é desenvolver uma indústria nacional”, declarou. O avanço da exploração de urânio, no entanto, depende de um debate maior sobre o setor nuclear prometido pelo ministro Alexandre Silveira (Minas e Energia) na última 6ª feira (6.nov). Segundo Silveira, o governo apresentará um plano de reestruturação do segmento ainda em 2026. Apesar de a reforma ter sido anunciada para e este ano, Arruda afirma que a discussão deve ficar para 2027. “O fato de o Urânio ter entrado na lista, na classe 1, demonstra que isso é uma atenção que o governo já está dando. Agora, nós precisamos, obviamente, a partir do novo governo Lula, sentar e definir como desenvolver isso”, declarou.

artigo.texto: Ex-employee sues OnderLaw, claims assault, online campaign for Ferguson data center ST. LOUIS, Mo. (First Alert 4) -An ex-employee of OnderLaw is suing the law firm, claiming harassment and an online campaign to sway public perception of a proposed data center in Ferguson. The lawsuit, filed on Thursday, was filed by an ex-employee referred to in court documents as Jane Doe. The lawsuit names the defendants as OnderLaw and James ‘Jim’ Onder. Onder’s lawyer told First Alert 4 he is declining to comment for the story. First Alert 4 has also reached out to OnderLaw for comment. As of publication time, we have not heard back. Court records show Onder’s lawyer had filed to have the case sealed by the court. In a Friday ruling, Judge Heather Cunningham denied the request. The 30-page lawsuit alleges a series of sexually inappropriate actions taken by Onder against Doe, along with allegations he pressured her to participate in a campaign against Ferguson and its city council regarding a vote against his proposed data center. The lawsuit alleges OnderLaw discriminated against Doe after she exercised her workers’ compensation rights and that the company violated Missouri’s whistleblower protection act. Against Onder himself, Doe alleges assault and battery The Ferguson Project On May 4, Ferguson’s City Council rejected tax breaks for Onder’s proposed data center at the former Emerson campus. The project would have received $1.5 billion in tax breaks over the 15 years of the agreement. After the rejection by the City Council, Doe claims that Onder ordered her to create a negative campaign about the city and residents. Onder told Doe the campaign would be pushed through Meta to residents in Ferguson; the content would appear as real news stories and paint the city as overrun with crime, the lawsuit states. The lawsuit says that Onder told Doe this would get him back to the approval process through a loophole and his relationships with officials and leaders at the Port Authority. Days after the rejection, on May 7, Doe was in a closed-door meeting with Onder, a St. Louis County official and a crisis public relations consultant. In this meeting, Doe alleged Onder again detailed his campaign plan. During the meeting, Onder said he wanted to instill fear about safety in Ferguson with exaggerated stories, making the data center “the only way out for these people,” documents state. While planning the campaign, Doe claims that Onder mocked Black people. Doe said during one meeting, while discussing what graphics to use during a Ferguson town hall, Onder said: “They [Black people] can’t read, so it doesn’t matter.” Doe says after the May 7 meeting she told Onder and Lisa Frederick, who served as the Chief Operating Officer, Chief Financial Officer, and President for OnderLaw, she would not work on the Ferguson project. Doe says that Onder persisted and told OnderLaw Director of Special Projects, Don Bertelsmann, to use bots to manufacture comments about Ferguson on social media that would look like they were coming from ordinary people. Doe alleges Onder instructed Bertelsmann to use computers in his home lab to do the botting. Months earlier, in January 2026, Doe alleges she was given a 2025 expense folder by Bertelsmann, showing a charge on his personal credit card for two “labs”; one at his house and another at his father-in-law’s house, according to the lawsuit. Bertelsmann wanted a reimbursement of $8,000 for equipment, software and internet service, the lawsuit states. At the time, Doe alleges that Bertelsmann wouldn’t tell her what the labs were for. Months later, Onder directed Bertelsmann to use his home lab and the computers in it to run bots for the Ferguson campaign. Allegations of violating Missouri lobbying law The lawsuit states that Onder’s goal was to influence Ferguson’s City Council’s decision on the data center’s tax breaks by pushing down real residents with fake accounts. The lawsuit states that Onder’s campaign efforts violated Missouri’s Lobbying Law, which requires every lobbyist to register with the Missouri Ethics Commission and prohibits hiring a person not registered as a lobbyist by the state. According to the lawsuit, Onder knew that Bertelsmann was not a registered lobbyist but still hired him. Doe claims she refused to be part of the campaign, as well as her team. She says she reported the campaign to Faith Earley, who was the firm’s new COO. The reports were done in mid-May; Doe says she reported her concerns multiple times after. The suit shows a text message exchange between Onder and Doe, in which Onder says, “So I shouldn’t announce to the World the illegal bribes each one requested to buy their votes?” in reference to the Ferguson City Council. Doe alleges repeated instances of sexually inappropriate behavior Doe claims in the lawsuit that Onder began acting sexually inappropriately toward her shortly after she joined his law firm in early 2025. The first incident happened, she claims, on April 2 of that year. She says Onder had touched her leg and waist after sitting next to her at a business meeting at a local steakhouse. She alleges in the suit she tried to move away from Onder, but couldn’t escape his reach and he continued the contact. A month later, on May 3, she alleges Onder began grabbing at her waist during an afternoon work party at an area hotel. She says Onder kept advancing on her until she was backed up against a wall. The suit alleges Onder had been pulling her so close that “he looked ready to kiss her.” Doe alleges she only got away after another party guest entered the room. The next month, between June 4 and 6, Doe claims she was on a work trip for OnderLaw. During the trip, she says Onder inappropriately touched her during a conference dinner. She claims Onder again inappropriately touched her leg again on the car ride back to their hotel. Doe alleges Onder asked her to go to the bar with him, which she refused. artigo.texto: ZTE Powers High Efficiency AIDC with Robust Energy Infrastructure AI's growth depends on stable, efficient, green energy—the foundation powering every model training run and inference call. November 11, 2026 Sponsored by ZTE As the AI wave surges forward, computing power is reshaping industries at an unprecedented pace. Yet behind every model training run and every inference call, what truly sustains continuous computing output is a stable, efficient, and green energy foundation. As per-rack power consumption climbs from 10–20 kW to 100 kW, 600 kW, and even 1 MW, as air cooling approaches its engineering limits and losses in traditional power supply links become increasingly prominent, the benchmark for AIDC competition is shifting from "computing scale" to "computing efficiency". In this "energy efficiency battle" crucial to the sustainable development of computing power, ZTE is reconstructing the "energy foundation" of AIDC with a systematic approach—ensuring every kilowatt-hour is converted into tokens more efficiently. Computing Power Sprints Ahead, Electricity Becomes a "Scarce Resource" Computing demand is growing explosively, and electricity consumption in computing centers is rising rapidly. The problem goes far beyond total electricity use: traditional data centers typically have a per-rack power consumption of 10–20 kW, while in the AIDC era, high-density deployment of GPU clusters has become the norm. Per-rack loads are quickly exceeding 100 kW, and high-end intelligent computing scenarios can reach 600 kW or even 1 MW. The shortcomings of traditional power supply architectures are now exposed: significant losses occur across the multi-stage conversion chain from transformer to server, resulting in extra annual operating costs. Such architectures can no longer meet the needs of high-density racks, making power supply architecture innovation urgent. Cooling challenges are equally severe: the engineering limit of air cooling is approximately 20–30 kW per rack, beyond which cooling capacity drops sharply. When the heat flux density of GPU clusters far exceeds the boundaries of air cooling, liquid cooling is no longer an "option" but a "mainstream solution"—the core guarantee for high-value computing power to operate stably at full load. The competitive benchmark for AIDC is shifting from "computing scale" to "computing efficiency". The long-term development of AI computing power increasingly depends on the upper limit of energy supply and on the end-to-end conversion efficiency from Energy to Token. This is precisely the core proposition ZTE is addressing. 800V High-Voltage DC System: Tackling Power Loss from the Source ZTE's first answer is the 800V high-voltage DC system, a fundamental innovation in traditional power supply architecture. With an efficient topology design, DC/DC intelligent battery management, diverse application modes, and excellent scalability, it delivers high-density, high-efficiency, green, and reliable DC power supply, solving the core power supply challenges of high-density computing infrastructure. Intelligent management has also achieved a leap forward: it supports one-stop full-link management and full-system visibility and controllability, covering functions such as fault recording, temperature measurement at key locations, and selective protection simulation. Predictive maintenance is carried out across three levels—module faults, system faults, and battery lifespan—making O&M more worry-free. Relying on dual-standard compatibility and modular elastic design, the system can flexibly switch voltage standards (±400V/800V), supporting smooth transition between old and new scenarios. Capacity can be expanded on demand, reducing initial investment pressure. It fully covers centralized large-scale computing bases and distributed edge computing upgrade scenarios, meeting the needs of all types of customers, including operators, internet companies, and professional computing power investors. Megawatt-Level Liquid Cooling CDU: Innovation Breaks Through the "Thermal" Ceiling While efficiency on the power supply side leaps forward, the cooling side also requires capability reconstruction. ZTE has launched a cold plate liquid cooling CDU to achieve optimal cooling costs across the full lifecycle and all-weather cooling safety assurance for equipment rooms. The CDU has a single-unit cooling capacity of 1.5 MW, expandable to 2.4 MW, with flexible configuration of 2–5 CDU cabinets. Auxiliary modules can be selected on demand and upgraded as business grows, greatly reducing initial investment and later retrofit waste. Based on the integration of multiple sensors for flow, pressure, temperature, and more, the 1500 kW liquid cooling CDU achieves precise temperature control of ±0.5°C and pressure control of ±0.05 bar, ensuring stable operation of high-density equipment. It is equipped with health indicators and status visualization for intelligent O&M, and features multiple safety designs such as N+X redundant hot backup and dual power feeds, supporting 7×24-hour uninterrupted operation. The combination of 800V high-voltage DC and the 1500 kW liquid cooling CDU outlines an efficient "inbound" and "outbound" channel for AIDC: the power supply side delivers every kilowatt-hour to the server with minimum loss, while the cooling side expels heat with maximum efficiency, keeping PUE stably within 1.15. Real-world application is the only benchmark for validating technological effectiveness. The Nanjing Binjiang Data Center was among the first to deliver demonstration results from its upgrade and transformation: It implemented a liquid-cooling integrated solution with a power density of up to 60 kW, adopting high-efficiency HVDC power distribution and busway, 32°C air supply, and group control optimization, achieving a PUE of only 1.15. artigo.texto: Hannah Pingree says she wants strict rules in place before data centers are built in Maine JAY (WGME) -- Developers of a proposed data center in the town of Jay say they've submitted permit applications to the Department of Environmental Protection. The local developer and its national partner, Sentinel Data Systems, have revived plans to replace the closed paper mill in Jay with a $550 million AI data center. However, Governor-Elect Hannah Pingree says strict rules must be in place before any data centers are built in Maine. "We have talked about implementing a moratorium until we have rules in place to protect ratepayers, to protect the environment and ensure community benefits. And that will continue to be my position," Pingree said. "The development of data centers in Maine without very strong regulations in place is not something that people are interested in." Developers plan to hold a public meeting next month in Jay to talk about the project. The governor-elect says she looks forward to learning more from the town and the developer about the proposed data center.

artigo.texto: O Partido Democrata assumirá o controle do Congresso e da maioria dos governos estaduais nos EUA em janeiro de 2026, após vencer as eleições de meio de mandato. A nova maioria planeja uma ofensiva rigorosa contra a expansão de data centers, inteligência artificial e as grandes empresas de tecnologia (big techs), motivada por preocupações com o meio ambiente e os altos custos de energia da rede elétrica. Quais são as principais medidas planejadas contra os data centers? Parlamentares democratas pretendem exigir que os operadores de grandes data centers arquem com uma fatia maior dos custos de melhorias na rede elétrica. Um projeto de lei em andamento visa agilizar novas usinas, mas impõe responsabilidades financeiras diretas às empresas. Além disso, nomes influentes, como o senador Bernie Sanders, defendem uma moratória nacional para impedir a construção de novas unidades. O argumento central é que essas estruturas consomem energia de forma desproporcional e podem prejudicar os consumidores comuns e o meio ambiente se não houver um controle rígido. Como a inteligência artificial será afetada pelas novas regras? A agenda democrata prioriza uma pausa no desenvolvimento de sistemas de inteligência artificial avançada e a proibição da chamada superinteligência. Deputados e senadores articulam propostas que exigem auditorias independentes para esses sistemas e formas de responsabilizar as empresas por eventuais danos causados pela tecnologia. Parlamentares reeleitos já sinalizaram que o primeiro dia do novo Congresso será marcado por intimações contra executivos das big techs, forçando o setor a prestar contas sobre o impacto de suas inovações na segurança nacional e na estabilidade social. Qual é a posição de Donald Trump sobre essas restrições tecnológicas? O presidente Donald Trump critica duramente as propostas da oposição e alega que esse cerco regulatório pode fazer os Estados Unidos perderem a corrida tecnológica para a China. Para o republicano, frear o avanço de data centers e da inteligência artificial é um erro estratégico que compromete a competitividade americana no cenário global. Após a vitória democrata nas midterms, que resultou em queda nas ações de empresas de tecnologia, Trump responsabilizou os eleitores, afirmando que a culpa pela instabilidade do mercado e pelo possível atraso tecnológico do país recai sobre eles. Existe o risco de as novas regras favorecerem a China? Analistas econômicos alertam que o fator decisivo na disputa com a China não é apenas o software, mas a capacidade computacional e a oferta de energia. Se a regulamentação se tornar uma barreira que impeça sistematicamente a construção de infraestrutura, os EUA podem perder espaço. Embora os democratas defendam que a fiscalização garante concorrência e segurança, o risco real é transformar leis em restrições de oferta. Caso o investimento seja desestimulado, a China poderá conquistar uma vantagem competitiva difícil de reverter, já que depende de energia e hardware para liderar a IA.
